transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess I'm here because work has just been getting really hard lately. My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at the salon. Like, even just doing basic stuff like sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. 

Which really sucks because color is usually my favorite thing to do. Actually, this one client came in on Tuesday wanting this super icy platinum blonde, which is honestly so hard to maintain, you know? Like, you have to use purple shampoo every single time you wash it or it gets super brassy. Plus she has well water at her house, so I told her it’s going to turn orange in like two weeks anyway. My aunt has well water and it completely ruined all her nice white towels. They’re all this weird rusty color now, and she was so mad because she bought them at Target, the really nice fluffy ones from that one specific brand... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, my hands just feel stuck. People at the salon have definitely started noticing I’m just way slower than I used to be, and I don't really know why.
Aside from feeling slower at work, have you noticed that you just don't enjoy doing the things you used to love anymore?

Yeah, I guess I have noticed that. I mean, I used to be super social. I’d always be chatting with my clients, or helping the newer stylists mix their formulas, and on my days off I’d always go hiking with my friends. We used to go up to this one trail by the reservoir all the time. Actually, it's closed right now because of a massive mudslide they had last month. My friend Jessica took her golden retriever up there right before they taped it off, and he got completely covered in mud. Like, literally brown from head to tail. She had to wash him in her apartment bathtub, and it clogged her drain so bad she had to call a plumber. Plumbers charge so much just to come out to your house now, it's crazy. She said it cost her like two hundred dollars just for him to snake the drain... 

But um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just... I don't really do any of that anymore. I just don’t have that spark in me. Now I mostly just keep my head down at my station and avoid people as much as I can.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, where you felt this low and unmotivated for weeks at a time?

Um, yeah, I think I have. Like, right now, most days I just wake up with this... this heavy, flat sadness in my chest. It just sits there. It feels like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, you know? I wanted to open my own salon by the time I was twenty-five. I even started looking at commercial spaces online. There was this really cute one downtown, right next to that new bakery that opened up. Have you been there? They make these amazing almond croissants, but they sell out by like 9 AM. My mom tried to go get me one for my birthday last year, but she got stuck in traffic because they were doing all that construction on Main Street. They took forever to finish those water lines, and it completely ruined the parking for all the businesses down there. The owner of the antique shop actually started a petition about it, but I don't think anything ever happened...

Wait, sorry. What was the question again? Oh, right, feeling low like this before. Yeah, I definitely have. It's just this heavy feeling that makes me not want to try anymore.

Have you ever had a period of time in your life where you felt the exact opposite of this—where you had an unusually high amount of energy, felt like you didn't need much sleep, or felt so wired that you were doing way more things than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I've never really had a time where I felt super energized or anything like that. I mean, I'm usually pretty tired anyway, especially since I'm on my feet all day at the salon. Some of the girls wear those really flat, unsupportive sneakers, like Converse or Vans, and I honestly don't know how they do it. I tried wearing my high-top Vans to work once because they looked really cute with my outfit—it was this vintage floral dress I found at a thrift store. Thrift shopping has gotten so expensive lately, though. Like, they're charging twenty dollars for a used t-shirt just because it's from the nineties. My brother actually found this original Nirvana shirt at a Goodwill once, and he sold it online for like two hundred bucks. He's always doing stuff like that, flipping clothes and shoes. He bought these limited edition sneakers...

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling wired or not sleeping. No, I've never really felt like that. I just feel tired and heavy most of the time.

You mentioned you've felt like this before; could you tell me how many distinct times in your life you've had a period of at least two weeks where you felt this same heavy, low, and unmotivated state?

Um, well, it's not really like it comes and goes in distinct times, you know? It's more like... it's just been there for a really long time. Like, I've had this heavy depression with me for about a year and two months now. It started right around the time the salon switched over to that new booking software. Oh my gosh, that software was a nightmare. They made us do this whole training seminar on a Sunday, which is supposed to be my day off, and the trainer they sent was this guy who kept talking about his cats. He had, like, five hairless cats, the Sphynx ones? He showed us all these pictures on his phone. I don't know, they kind of creep me out, they look like raw chicken. My aunt used to have a Persian cat, the really fluffy ones, and it shed everywhere. She had to buy this special vacuum just for pet hair, the Dyson one. Those Dysons are so expensive, but I guess they work really well. She said she could vacuum a whole rug and the canister would be completely full of white hair...

Wait, sorry. The question. How many times have I felt this way? Yeah, it's not really separate times. It's just been this one long stretch for about a year and two months. It just hasn't gone away.
During this year and two months that you've been feeling this way, have you also struggled with changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep?

Um, yeah, actually. My appetite has been really weird. I've been skipping meals without really meaning to. Like, I'll just realize at night that all I've had all day is coffee and maybe a few bites of something. Which reminds me, the coffee machine at the salon has been broken for like three weeks, and the manager refuses to get it fixed. She says we should just bring our own from home, but who has time for that in the morning? I used to stop at this little drive-thru place on my way in, but they raised their prices so much. A regular iced latte is like six dollars now. Can you believe that? And they use that cheap oat milk that separates when you pour it in. My roommate tried making her own oat milk once. She bought this huge bag of oats from Costco and soaked them overnight, but she didn't strain it right, so it was all slimy and gross. She ended up throwing the whole batch away. Costco is crazy on the weekends, anyway. People get so aggressive over those free samples. I saw two ladies arguing over the last piece of a frozen pizza once...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, my appetite. Yeah, so I just haven't been eating much, mostly just coffee. I've definitely noticed my clothes have gotten looser lately.
